page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. The configuration includes 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity stands at 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a 300 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the instance has a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6870.73 and a PassMark CPU score of 7626.07. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1155.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1304.38. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 382.09 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 51.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 6.38 million operations per second, while database operations on PassMark are weak at 2587.31. LLM inference speeds are weak to poor, particularly for 7B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r5dn.2xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with local NVMe storage, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-core compute performance. The primary tradeoff is the lower single-threaded processing speed. This instance is configured for workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and memory-intensive data processing tasks that benefit from dedicated vCPUs and local high-speed storage.
